tabs.title: Who they are
tabs.description: Getting to know Farah (37, sustainability consultant) & Salman Khureshi (39, insurance-sector data scientist) — professions that make them constitutionally incapable of ignoring tail risk, and a 2022 flood that drowned their car, their deposit, and any tolerance for unverified ground.

buyers.name: Farah Khureshi
buyers.description: Asks for STP maintenance logs (sales offices now warn each other), verifies rainwater harvesting is real, and instituted the joy rule: any property that passes the maps gets evaluated on light and life like a normal home. The final gate is a mango tree and east sun.

chatMessages.text: The approach road, Riya, is currently auditioning as a canal. Ten out of ten flow rate. The 'high ground' starts fifty metres AFTER the water feature, yaar.

Then that's a fail — access floods are still floods; ask anyone who couldn't reach their dry house in 2022. And the ridge-side one from last week? Your notes said the basement ramp shed water like it was designed by someone who'd actually seen rain. The joy rule passes it — ridge-side goes to offer. Bring the umbrella home.

filters.title: THE 2022 CONVERSION

filters.title: THE INVERTED MARKET LOGIC
filters.description: They treat '10 minutes from ORR' as a risk disclosure, not an amenity — the employment spine runs along the city's lowest, most lake-filled corridor, and they are consciously long safety.

filters.title: THE BROCHURE HYDROLOGY
filters.description: Every 'flood-proof' claim is a brochure bullet — the ₹50K commissioned report per finalist remains the line item they defend most cheerfully.

filters.title: THE EVANGELISM BURDEN
filters.description: They can't unknow what they know — every friend's lakebed purchase presents the quiet dilemma: say something and strain the friendship, or stay silent and watch the 2022 photos repeat.

tabs.filtersFooterLabel: They were filtering for verified elevation, functioning STP logs, quantified water security, and a monsoon that has seen each finalist in real rain.
tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “The Khureshis taught me that the water remembers every one of the 180+ lakes the city built over — and so do they. The public data stack eliminated 60% of the inventory in an afternoon; the ₹50K hydrology reports were for finalists, not the funnel. The monsoon protocol re-ranked the shortlist twice — one 'high ground' approach road performed as a canal, and access floods are still floods. And the discipline that saved them from analysis-forever was Farah's joy rule: any property that passes the maps gets evaluated on light and life like a normal home. The winner passed the maps and the light test — east morning sun, a mango tree older than the project. They're buying high ground, not a bunker, and the file now contains one photograph that isn't evidence.”

differentlyCards.title: Run the data stack before the first site visit
differentlyCards.description: The 60% grey-out happened in month one — had the stack been built pre-search, the funnel would have been clean from the first Sunday.

differentlyCards.title: Schedule the monsoon protocol in the needs card
differentlyCards.description: The canal-performing approach road was discovered at month five — 'see each finalist in real rain' should have been a gate from the start, not a refinement.

differentlyCards.title: Commission hydrology with the shortlist, not after
differentlyCards.description: The ₹50K reports arrived at month four — commissioning with the first shortlist would have greyed out two of the three finalists sooner.

differentlyCards.title: Write the joy rule on the first page
differentlyCards.description: Farah's rule was instituted at month six — the layer-stack's veto had been running unchecked for five months, and joy deserved a vote from day one.

chatMessages.text: The basement sheds rain like a design decision, the tanker dependence is under twenty percent, and there's an old mango tree in the morning sun. Even the layer-stack approves of the light.

That's the file complete — maps, reports, monsoon photos, and one photograph that isn't evidence. The water remembers, and so do you. But the house you chose was always going to be the one where joy passed the final gate.

tabs.adviceDescription: For climate-aware buyers, the method is the margin: screen the funnel with public data — flood maps, lake buffers, valley lines — and spend the commissioned report on finalists only. Verify under-construction drainage mid-build, visit every finalist in real rain with approach roads included, and ask the 2022 WhatsApp-photo question, because both answers are complete. Price the elevation premium and the flood-zone discount honestly, and remember the joy rule: any property that passes the maps gets evaluated on light and life like a normal home. Farah and Salman proved that buying high ground is not a bunker — it's a home on the highest contour, with one photograph in the file that isn't evidence.
